title.narrative: Joining Efforts for an Education of Excellence in Paraguay Project

description.narrative: The Project aims at improving learning conditions and strengthening institutional frameworks in core priority areas of the education system in Paraguay, all in support of the Ministry of Education and Sciences (MEC)'s strategy to significantly improve the quality of education in Paraguay in the next two decades. To achieve this goal, the Project Development Objective (PDO) is articulated around two clear objectives. First, to significantly improve learning environments in targeted "upgradable compulsory education institutions" (UCEIs) and to adapt infrastructure of selected teacher training institutes (IFDs, in their Spanish acronym) that will be converted into university-level degree-granting Experimental Centers for Specialized Teacher Training (CEFEDs, in their Spanish acronym). Second, to strengthen institutional frameworks that have been identified by MEC as core priority areas for improving education service delivery, namely the areas of: (i) educational infrastructure; (ii) the use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) for Education (henceforth, EdTech); (iii) the development of a new teaching profession through the introduction of specialized pre-service teacher training in key thematic - numeracy, literacy, social sciences, and natural sciences - and specific transversal - intercultural education, early childhood education - areas; and (iv) institutional assessment tools. The first objective of the PDO will be supported under Component 1, and the second objective will be supported under Component 2.The objective of Component 1 is to support the GoP in improving learning environments in Paraguay through a comprehensive suite of structural interventions. This goal is framed within an overarching policy that aims to revamp the material - structural and pedagogical - conditions under which learning takes place in Paraguay. The “intervention package” to be provided to learning environments in these institutions will comprise: (i) civil works; (ii) learning materials; (iii) educational equipment, including digital devices, as needed; (iv) furniture; and (v) Internet connectivity.The objective of Component 2 will be to support, through both technical assistance and capacity building activities, in developing high-quality institutional frameworks around the four aforementioned thematic areas. Institutional frameworks to be strengthened comprise: (i) learning environments and educational infrastructure standards; (ii) EdTech competency frameworks; (iii) teachers professional career and development; and (iv) institutional assessment tools.

To improve learning environments in selected schools and teacher training institutions, strengthen institutional frameworks in core priority areas, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

condition.narrative: Section I: Implementation ArrangementsA. Institutional Arrangements1. The Borrower, through MEC, shall operate and maintain, atall times throughout Project implementation, the Project implementation unit (“UEPP”), with functions and responsibilitiesacceptable to the Bank, which shall be responsible for overall Project coordination and technical oversight of the Project, andstaffed with competent personnel in adequate numbers, with qualifications, experience and terms of reference satisfactory to theBank, as set forth in the Operational Manual.

Section I: Implementation ArrangementsA. Institutional Arrangements2. The Borrower, through MEC, shall, no later than ninety(90) days after the Effective Date, hire or appoint, as applicable, the following additional staff as part of the UEPP: (i) aProject manager; (ii) an UCEI coordinator, in charge of overseeing overall interventions with respect to UCEIs; (iii) a CEFEDcoordinator, in charge of overseeing overall interventions with respect to IFDs to be converted to CEFEDs; (iv) an infrastructurecoordinator, in charge of the general supervision of infrastructure-related activities; (v) an ICT coordinator, in charge of thegeneral supervision of ICT-based activities; (vi) a senior accountant; (vii) a junior accountant; (viii) a senior financialmanagement specialist; (ix) a junior financial management specialist; (x) a senior procurement specialist; (xi) a juniorprocurement specialist; (xii) a monitoring and evaluation specialist; (xiii) a design and structural calculations specialist; and(xiv) an electricity specialist; all with qualifications, experience and terms of reference satisfactory to the Bank, as set forthin the Operational Manual.

Section I: Implementation ArrangementsB. Operational Manual1. Without limitation to the provisions of Section 3.01 of thisAgreement, the Borrower, through MEC, shall carry out the Project in accordance with the provisions of a manual (“OperationalManual), acceptable to the Bank, which shall include, inter alia: (a) the procedures for the carrying out, monitoring andevaluation of the Project, including performance indicators; (b) detailed institutional arrangements for the Project, including thecomposition, functions and responsibilities of the UEPP; (c) the criteria for the selection of UCEIs and CIESs under Part 1of theProject and IFDs under Part 1.2 of the Project; (d) the criteria for the provision and implementation of Grants under Part1.1(a)(ii) of the Project; (e) the Project's procurement, financial management, and disbursement requirements and procedures; (f)the stakeholder engagement plan, grievance mechanism, and code of conduct; (g) the Anti-Corruption Guidelines and procedures toensure compliance with the Anti-Corruption Guidelines; and (h) the ESCP.
